description: iOS/macOS/web dev building a native ios game for the Space Mission Design Game challenge
summary:
Mission Tycoon is a cozy 3D browser game that turns space mission design into something you can feel. You run a small space agency on a run-down island spaceport. A client posts a job, like photographing the coast or watching northern forests for wildfires, and you design the mission to deliver it. You buy or order parts and build a CubeSat while six live budgets push back against every choice: mass, power, money, data, communications and time. Then you pick an orbit, a rocket and ground stations, and face a GO/NO-GO poll from your crew. You fly the launch yourself through ignition, staging and the final burn into orbit. Then you run the mission day by day as your photos squeeze through the radio, solar storms hit and fires flare.

Every result is explained. The mission report gives the three real reasons your mission succeeded or fell short, how to fix each one, and the real NASA mission yours most resembles. A free test run and “Fix and relaunch” make it safe to fail and try again.
details:
Space Mission Tycoon is a cozy 3D space-agency builder that runs in the browser, where every number on screen is a real mission-design trade-off.

WHAT IT DOES

You run a small, run-down space agency on an old island spaceport. A client posts a job with a science target, a deadline and a fee. You buy parts at the market, build a satellite on a 3D turntable, and watch six live bars: mass, power, budget, data, communications and time. Each bar explains itself in one plain sentence when it turns red. A free test run predicts the result. Then you choose an orbit, a rocket and ground stations, hear a GO / NO-GO call from four crew seats, and fly the launch yourself or on autopilot. In orbit you watch the data pile up and squeeze through the radio, and make decisions when things go wrong. The report gives 0 to 3 stars, the top three reasons the mission went the way it did, what would fix it, and the closest real NASA mission. Then you fix the design and fly again. Satellites keep sending raw data, a Science Lab turns it into products, and the money restores the spaceport.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Mission design is usually taught with spreadsheets. We wanted students and curious players to feel the trade-offs instead: why a bigger camera needs more power, why a satellite needs a battery for the 35 minutes of shadow on every orbit, why data is useless if the radio cannot bring it home. Failure is allowed, even launching over a NO-GO, and it is always explained. It needs no install and no account.

HOW I BUILT IT

TypeScript, React, three.js (react-three-fiber), zustand and Vite, deployed on GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions. The rules engine is plain TypeScript with 57 unit tests, and all balancing lives in data tables. The 3D models are built in code, and the music and sound effects are synthesised in the browser with the Web Audio API, so there are no model or audio files.

CREATIVITY AND WHAT WE CONSIDERED

It looks like a farm-builder, but the game underneath is the mission design. We weighed accuracy against simplicity: the numbers are game values, but each rule is a simplified real one. We kept the words plain, added a guided first flight with our instructor, Chief Rocco, a Reduce motion setting and a Fast mode for judges.

USE OF AI

The character images were generated with ChatGPT. We used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI coding assistant throughout: it wrote and fixed some code under my direction, including the code that generates the music and sound effects.
